=== page 9 ===
- The most significant improvements are observed at a nanoparticle volume concentration of 1.25%, resulting in an average increase of 37.83% compared with pure water at the three different mass flow rates.
- For lower concentrations, the average increases in heat transfer are 7.16% at 0.25%, 15.47% at 0.50%, 23.32% at 0.75%, and 30.76% at 1.00%.
- The percentage difference between the lowest and highest mass flow rates reaches approximately 35.64% for the nanofluid with a nanoparticle volume concentration of 1.25%.
- The presence of nanoparticles improves the thermal conductivity of the coolant, thereby facilitating a more efficient heat transfer.^32 However, the highest percentage increase occurs across all nanofluid mass flow rates when the nanoparticle volume concentration is 1.25%, as shown in Figure 5.
- Compared with water, this increase corresponds to an average of 47.84%.
- Additionally, for lower concentrations, the increase is 8.51% at 0.25%, 18.70% at 0.50%, 28.62% at 0.75%, and 38.32% at 1.00%.
- The pressure drop increases by 1.72% at 0.25%, 2.61% at 0.50%, 3.51% at 0.75%, and 4.41% at 1.00% volume concentrations.
- For instance, at a mass flow rate of 0.7 kg/s, the pumping power increased from 1,742W for water to 1,768W for the 1.25% nanofluid, corresponding to an increase of approximately 1.5%.
- At a nanoparticle volume concentration of 1.25%, the Al2O3/water nanofluid increased the heat transfer rate and heat transfer coefficient by 37.83% and 47.84%, respectively, while the pressure drop increased by only 5.30% and the pumping power by approximately 1.5%.
- Similar observations were reported by Singh, Verma, and Ghosh,^115 who investigated the thermal performance of an industrial heat exchanger using graphene-based nanofluids at concentrations of 0.1%, 0.25%, 0.5%, 0.75%, and 1.0%.
